cpu_conclusion: C95 eliminates boundary blob command replay but leaves all observed column-map, anchor-map and footprint lookup event counts unchanged in every case. Standard-Nether process CPU in root evaluation is mixed (-2.77% main, +1.64% second seed); normal-build adverse CPU remains unresolved. Fire and soul-fire stages include recursive earlier-state generation. Top root does not mean exclusive feature placement or an isolated removable cost.
memory_conclusion: The earlier C95 +30.69% Overworld high-water observation is not repeated: this run reverses its direction. Current RSS rises 842 MiB for C94 versus 124 MiB for C95 during twenty measured regions, after almost equal post-warmup RSS. Completed GPU jobs during measured generation differ 66 versus 68, with one extra job each in regions 2 and 14. Aggregate logical upload is identical and readback differs by 224 bytes. Every measured region is shader-ready, and warmup job counts match. The counter increments at completed GPU sample publication and excludes warmup jobs in this harness; the cause of these extra small requests is unconfirmed. Neither a leak nor the cause of allocator/driver residency is identified. Prior adverse results remain retained. Twenty regions do not establish a sustained plateau.

source_review.column_traversal: Planner::column first checks completed interior version skips and exterior reuse, then ready_columns/sharded boundary tile lookup. build_column recursively calls prefix for prior roots. C95 only changes how eligible output-column commands are consumed.
source_review.existing_material_membership: placement/materials.rs already compiles suitable material sets to bitsets and specializes short lists. Adding another generic membership cache is not a new opportunity.
source_review.existing_view_cache: ViewColumns already caches exact-key immutable prior columns within a view, including collision fallback. Any new reuse experiment must measure what remains outside those paths.
source_review.overworld: Zero ordered dependency roots in both observer cases. Only dependencies.rs and output_columns.rs differ in the held native trees; GPU and Overworld implementation files are identical. This does not establish that process memory/scheduling must be identical.

limits: Instrumentation is part of measured evaluation. Other inactive test hooks still differ from a normal release; C95 removes some inactive per-command probe calls along with command replay. An instrumented improvement cannot explain or reverse a normal-build adverse result by itself.
Per-root stages identify where work is triggered, including earlier roots reconstructed on demand. They are not exclusive feature-placement attribution.

Overworld uses no ordered dependency roots here. This observer cannot attribute its high-water memory increase.
